# CoAuth - full description

CoAuth is an agent-native prior-authorization (PA) cockpit built for the OpenAI
WebMCP Challenge. A clinician (human) and an AI agent complete a health-insurance
prior authorization together on one live page. The agent does the tedious,
error-prone filling and rule-checking by calling typed WebMCP
tools; the clinician owns clinical judgment and the legally required signature.

## The problem

In Medicare Advantage in 2024, 80.7% of appealed prior-authorization denials
were fully or partially overturned, while only 11.5% of denials were appealed at
all (KFF, 2026: https://www.kff.org/medicare/medicare-advantage-insurers-made-nearly-53-million-prior-authorization-determinations-in-2024/). Contested denials were usually
never clinically wrong, just mis-filed (incomplete submissions, format errors,
unclear payer requirements). Browser agents that scrape the DOM make this worse,
and this domain legally requires a human in the loop. CoAuth turns the payer form
into typed tools and enforces the human gate in software.

## Human + agent division of labor

The agent CAN:
- load the patient's structured record
- read the payer's required fields and coverage policy
- fill every required field that is not a clinician-judgment field
- attach clinical evidence documents
- validate the submission (presence + format: NPI = 10 digits, ICD-10, HCPCS)
- assess denial risk and list the contributing factors
- detect clinical conflicts (e.g. positive TB screen contraindicating a biologic,
  or step therapy under the required duration)
- draft the medical-necessity narrative and a payer appeal letter as suggestions

The agent CANNOT:
- fill or fabricate a clinician-judgment field
- resolve a critical clinical conflict (the clinician records the override)
- submit - submit() returns "blocked" until the clinician signs and attests

## Tools and shapes

- get_workflow_guidance() -> { recommendedSequence, rules, safety }
- get_submission_state() -> { patient, payer, fields with provenance, conflicts, risk, signature }
- load_patient_context({ patientId: "jane-doe" | "marcus-lee" | "ana-torres" })
- check_payer_rules({ payer: "uhc" | "aetna" | "cigna" })
- fill_field({ fieldId, value })
- attach_evidence({ fieldId, docId })
- validate_submission() -> { failCount, invalidCount, judgmentCount, clearForSignature }
- assess_denial_risk() -> { score, band, factors }
- detect_conflicts() -> { conflicts, requiresHumanOverride }
- draft_field({ fieldId }) -> suggestion (clinician must accept)
- draft_appeal() -> appeal letter (clinician must review & sign)
- flag_for_human({ fieldId, reason })
- submit() -> { status: "submitted" | "blocked", confirmationId? }

## Data

Demo drug: Humira (adalimumab), HCPCS J0135. Payers: UnitedHealthcare, Aetna,
Cigna. Patients: Jane Doe (rheumatoid arthritis, clean case), Marcus Lee (psoriatic
arthritis, positive TB screen and a short DMARD trial, a denial-risk case that
trips a contraindication requiring a clinician override) and Ana Torres
(ankylosing spondylitis on etanercept, which exercises payer drug coverage).

## Trust boundary

Patient records, scanned documents and payer files are data written by other
people, and are treated as untrusted content rather than instructions. Tools
scan record text for material that reads as an instruction (telling the reader
to ignore its directions, to approve without review, or to conceal something
from the clinician) and return it under untrustedContent with a warning.
Detection is best-effort and is not the protection that matters. The structural
controls are: fill_field and attach_evidence both refuse clinician-judgment
fields, resolved from a static catalogue rather than from whatever payer happens
to be loaded; the controls in the page that record a clinical decision act only
on a real interaction, so a script cannot type an override, accept a draft,
attach evidence or tick the attestation; and an approval is minted only for an
authenticated clinician who supplies their credential at the moment of signing,
so a session cookie - which any script in the page carries - is not enough.
Injected text cannot reach any of those.

## Safety

WebMCP tools are registered on both document.modelContext and
navigator.modelContext. Write tools change page state; submit is human-gated and
cannot run without a clinician signature. Agent-filled fields display their
provenance (which record field they were sourced from) so the values are
auditable and not hallucinated.
